tasks.title: Prove public-API fork composition
tasks.objective: Build one deliberately small fork-and-combine example using only public APIs without moving scheduling or evaluation into ctxmux.
tasks.outcome: A client can express a bounded Crucible- or MapReduce-like workflow while the runtime remains a mux rather than a Harness.
acceptance: The example creates, forks, observes, stops, and combines Runs using only public client and Integration APIs.
Scheduling, evaluation, reduction, winner selection, and stopping policy remain inside the example client.
The example is deterministic enough for the repository gate and does not create a reusable orchestration framework.

verification.proves: The public composition example and full repository checks pass.

tasks.title: Prepare reproducible installation and release gates
tasks.objective: Make binaries and packages installable and release-checkable with public claims bounded to proven behavior, without publishing externally.
tasks.outcome: Ctxmux is release-ready through reproducible local checks and accurate installation and compatibility documentation.
acceptance: Rust binaries and the TypeScript package have reproducible build, install, package-content, and compatibility checks.
README and package metadata distinguish current native, fork, persistence, and tmux guarantees accurately.
Release preparation performs no registry publish, Git push, hosted release, or other external mutation without explicit authorization.

verification.proves: Packaging, installation, compatibility, composition, and full repository checks pass.
Public positioning and installation guidance describe only shipped capabilities.
